thread:
mira: Quick heads-up — hitting a repeatable drift with nova-10b on the q4_kv quant path. After ~3000 tokens the logits shift and output degenerates, fp16 run looks fine. Logs below.
ryan: can you share the run id / repro? curious if it's RoPE wrapping or KV corruption. :thinking:
mira: run: https://ci.internal/runs/98532 (private) — repro command:
```
./serve_local --model nova-10b --quant q4_kv --context 4096 --seed 13 --prompt-file long_session.txt
```
Log excerpt (approx token idx 2989 -> 3010):
```
[2026-03-18T16:02:13Z] kv_replay: next_idx=2989 expected_pos=2989
[2026-03-18T16:02:13Z] kv_replay: wrote_entry len=64 header=0x1f
[2026-03-18T16:02:13Z] kv_restore: next_idx=2989 got_pos=0   <-- oops
[2026-03-18T16:02:13Z] generation: logits unexpected spike, tok=2989->a_noise
```
jess: that line `got_pos=0` looks like header offset misread — could be serialization endian or extra padding introduced by new quant packer. Did we run binary-compat tests between q4_kv and the KV format consumer?
carol: onboarding checklist question — is this only on nova-10b or other archs? have we tried veridian7b or zenith13b with same q4_kv path?
mira: quick matrix: veridian7b q4_kv shows no issue. zenith13b hasn't been tested yet. seems model-arch specific, nova-10b has rotary layer count parity that might interact with our packer.
ryan: possible RoPE phase shift if the kv entries are misaligned by even 1 element. Two things to check: (1) drop-in run with `--kv-compat=legacy` to force old serializer; (2) compare raw kv blob hashes before/after quant path.
mira: ran `--kv-compat=legacy` — no regression. So likely the q4_kv serializer is the culprit.
jess: can you dump hexdiff of the blob header? even a single-byte shift would point to header struct mismatch. Example command:
```
xxd -g 1 kv_blob.bin | sed -n '1,40p'
```
mira: dump snippet (hexdump):
```
00000000: 10 02 00 00 04 3c ...  <-- expected magic 0x02 0x10 on old path
00000008: 20 00 00 00 40 00 ...
```
mira: noticed header bytes are swapped relative to legacy; looks like endianness flip when quant packer writes header len.
ryan: aha. that matches `got_pos=0` — code reading header as little-endian got a huge length and wrapped. Likely introduced by `q4_packer.c` change in commit `f8c3b2d` where we refactored into memcpy with no host-order normalization.
carol: recommended triage steps:
- run bisection between `abc123`..`f8c3b2d` on q4_kv packer
- add unit test roundtrip for header endianness
- verify zenith13b and nova-10b parity
- create a short eval to catch logits drift (prompt corpus: long_session.txt)
infra-bot: scheduled job #4898: eng-ml/bisect-q4-kv for nova-10b (owner: ryan)
ryan: taking owner. I'll run bisect locally then schedule GPU runs. first bisect cmd:
```
git bisect start -- nova-main
git bisect bad f8c3b2d
git bisect good abc123
```
jess: if bisect points to packer change, add a reproduction unit in `tests/kv_compat_test.cc` that asserts `memcmp(header, expected, 8) == 0` across both packers.
mira: also adding an eval harness: `evals/drift_detection/nova_long_context.json` to fail fast on regressions.
ryan: I'll post updates in this thread. If anyone spots a quick patch for endian normalization, ping me. :thumbsup:
mira: thanks — repro gist attached: https://gist.internal/nova-q4-kv-repro
ryan: kicked off bisect job, will update with commit when found — ETA ~ 2h.
carol: great triage, keep the ticket linked (INF-2147).
